sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: Connect opposing BCL-2-family roles to outer-mitochondrial-membrane permeabilization and the two linked caspase routes.
sourceFitAssessment.gap: The existing Mermaid is a useful mechanistic route map, including the BID cross-link; it should be retained. Its pore and cytochrome-c boxes do not locate the mitochondrial membrane or show release, so a small physical inset can clarify the defining event without replacing the route topology.
accuracyGuardrails: One mitochondrial route is not every kind of death.
Abundance is not dependency; do not rank inhibitor efficacy.
Apoptosis does not automatically establish immunogenicity.
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: The complete accepted owner connects the three opposing BCL-2-family groups in its table and explanation to the new physical outer-membrane inset. The inset, alt and adjacent explanation locate cytochrome c on the intermembrane-space side of the inner membrane and its release through the outer membrane into the cytosol, resolving the frozen spatial gap. The retained Mermaid supplies both the intrinsic stress-to-caspase route and the death-receptor/caspase-8 route, including the BID cross-link; the inset explicitly supplements that topology. The full page also retains the abundance-versus-dependency exercise, route-limited BAX/BAK interpretation, compound-selectivity boundary and separate immunogenicity discussion. Taken together, this supports the whole frozen learner task, including its guardrails, rather than only the new inset.
